docs.purpose: The form on which an operator assigns a specific advertiser to a specific advertising slot in the product — which sponsor appears where, and for how long. The list of valid slots is a closed, declared set rather than free text, so a placement cannot be pointed at a slot that does not exist. Today the component that would display a sponsor renders nothing at all, so there is no way to sell or schedule a placement.
docs.data_story: It writes one offers row (created inactive) and one admin_audit_log row per save through the offer contract; the advertiser select lists the active advertisers from the placements read.
docs.under_126: **GENERATED.** Rendered by the web FORM binding (RJSF with the Mantine theme) from render.form and offer_request in placements-contract.json; the advertiser select takes its options from the placements read (options_from, the shared binding standard). The SLOT this configures is still not served (D-7).

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM offers WHERE flight_end IS NOT NULL AND flight_start IS NOT NULL AND flight_end < flight_start
invariants.why: A flight that ends before it starts renders zero impressions while reading as scheduled — an advertiser paying for nothing, invisible in every count.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM offers o WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM placements p WHERE p.placement_key = o.placement_key)
invariants.why: The closed placement vocabulary is the point: an offer pointed at a slot that does not exist can never render, and the FK plus this assertion are what make "never a literal" true.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT o.placement_key, count(*) AS n FROM offers o WHERE o.active GROUP BY 1) x JOIN placements p USING (placement_key) WHERE x.n > p.max_slots
invariants.why: max_slots is the declared cap the SLOT archetype renders against; oversubscription is a commercial state an operator may create deliberately, so it warns rather than fails — but it is never silent.

plausibility.sql: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT disclosure_required), count(*) FROM placements
plausibility.why: Any placement rendering to a user without disclosure_required is a legal exposure, not a preference; the expected count is zero and a non-zero one is a defect rather than a signal.

notes: MF-40 (plan delta 1, option C; the four trims). The offer FORM of the admin placements page. No disclosure field (placements is seed-only); no active field (offers save inactive and toggle from the offers list, trim 4); no zone_class (serving row, trim 1); no image picker (ad contract v2, trim 2). building_type and design_option are static selects; which a placement accepts and the scenario_card pair are checked by the route (the media precedent: conditionals in the route).
